EPA growth rate quantifies positional effectiveness over time, revealing that TEs have gained value while FBs have declined. Field position distribution encodes spatial bias in pass selection, aligning with game theory where drives begin closer to midfield. These primitives form a dual framework: one temporal (growth rates), one spatial (distribution). Each is susceptible to confounding variables such as coaching philosophy, QB skill, and team scheme. Failure modes include overfitting to outlier seasons or misrepresenting non-linear changes in usage patterns. The interplay between these operators reveals a dynamic system where position roles evolve through strategic adaptation rather than static evolution.
